newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand dollar settled in mid range at close.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand dollar settled in mid range at close.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar finished the week on Friday in the middle of its session range and dealers doubt it will stray too far over the weekend.
It closed at 5.00 p.m. (0500 GMT) at US$0.6910/17 after trading a 0.6910-26 range and opening at 0.6913/20.
The Trade-Weighted Index ended a little firmer at 68.24 from the 68.20 opening.

Dealers said the focus next week will be on the U.S. dollar and Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee meeting. But even if the expected quarter point rise in U.S. rates eventuates, New Zealand's interest rate differentials are still viewed
favourably and the hike should not unduly affect the kiwi.
A Wellington bank chief dealer said the New Zealand dollar had performed well on Friday in the face of Australian dollar weakness, which was attributed to Japanese and U.S. investor selling.
"The Aussie is still looking rather sick but the kiwi has only edged lower, and it looks okay. I think the Aussie will lose ground against the U.S. but the kiwi will outperform it."
He said there was genuine interest to buy the New Zealand dollar from Australian and U.S. buyers.
